A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same paired latent-diffusion seismic synthesis work, with matching core equations and SCEDC experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including figures, tables and equations; v2 extends and reorganizes the material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCEDC synthesis experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations, waveform analyses and supplementary examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original SCEDC results and reports additional KMA and INSTANCE experiments, magnitude manipulation and further ablations.

M1.justification: HEGGS names the existing paired-data diffusion method. Equations (1)-(9), the conditional U-Net, end-to-end objective and amplitude correction module are retained. v1's architecture description moves to v2 Appendix B.1; Appendix J clarifies training and inference without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from Southern California SCEDC data to South Korean KMA and Italian INSTANCE data. Section 4.2.4 also evaluates deliberately altered earthquake magnitudes without a source waveform, a fictitious-event scenario discussed but not experimentally demonstrated in v1.

E2.justification: The four SCEDC baseline families remain SeismoGen, ConSeisGen, BBGAN and LDM. v2 Table 2 adds a paired-input BBGAN attempt reported as diverged, while Table 3 adds LDM+ACM comparisons with and without paired training. The new regional benchmarks compare HEGGS with the existing LDM baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces dataset-specific filtering, splits, EQT fine-tuning, normalization and regional GMPE calculations, plus magnitude-manipulation and unnormalized-LDM control protocols. Existing SCEDC coordinate bounds also change: latitude normalization uses 32.024809-36.151200 in v1 Equation (12), versus 32.0-37.9 in v2 Table 5, with longitude bounds revised too. This establishes a reported setting change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds controls testing whether ACM enables conventional LDM to handle unnormalized waveforms and how paired training contributes independently of end-to-end training. Figure 6 adds controlled magnitude manipulation and spectral-response analysis. Regional frequency and virtual-station analyses expand, while the appendix retains fewer SCEDC positive and negative ablation examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and retain the statement that SeismoGen and ConSeisGen results reflect the best performance across 30 iterations. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing SCEDC Table 2 scores, the original four Table 3 rows and VAE reconstruction scores remain unchanged. v2 adds regional results, two ablation rows, BBGAN divergence and magnitude-response findings. For example, HEGGS with source input reports P/S MAE of 0.2763/0.4644 seconds on KMA. These are new results, not improved SCEDC scores. Table 1 removes the earlier precision and recall entries.

T1.justification: The core transformation assumption, paired-loss argument and reverse-process reasoning in Equations (1)-(9) are retained. Appendix J expands standard diffusion formulas and restates that argument rather than supplying a substantively new proof or assumption. Appendix F documents regional evaluation formulas.

C1.justification: The principal contribution remains high-fidelity seismic synthesis using paired diffusion training and minimal conditions. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion broaden the stated dataset-construction and validation scope from SCEDC to three geographic regions, while foregrounding end-to-end and single-GPU learning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets ACM as enabling unnormalized conventional-LDM training and adds mechanism explanations concerning source noise and diffusion time in Appendix J. Discussion adds qualifications about missing geological information for fictitious events and consistency across regional models. It removes v1's specific discussion of failures above magnitude 5, high-frequency deficiencies above 10 Hz and distant-station artifacts.

D1.justification: v2 adds regional data-selection and normalization recipes, explicit GMPE coefficients and assumptions, similarity-normalization disclosures, and training/inference pseudocode specifying optional source-waveform initialization. Existing hardware, optimizer and training-budget details are retained. Conversely, v1's explicit detrending and unknown-instrument-response exclusion descriptions are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for KMA and INSTANCE, regional magnitude/GMPE calculations and magnitude scaling, including Han, Michelini, Di Bona, Emolo, Lanzano, Sheen and Geller. Positioning relative to GAN synthesis, LDM, TANGO and MP-SeNet remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and discussion are substantially rewritten, Problem Statement and Seismic Dataset are consolidated into Key Idea, and architecture details move into the appendices. Evaluation is organized around three generation scenarios, with expanded explanatory material in Appendix J and consistent HEGGS terminology.

P2.justification: Tables gain regional groupings, Figures 2-5 become regional comparisons, and magnitude-manipulation and algorithm displays are added. Appendix galleries are substantially reduced and reorganized. Spectrogram axes also change from approximately 0-60 seconds and 0-50 Hz to 0-6 seconds and 0-3000 Hz in Figure 4 and Appendix H, conflicting with the stated data duration and sampling.

improvement.justification: Korean and Italian evaluations substantially strengthen v1's single-region evidence base, while the added ACM controls better distinguish component contributions. Regional protocols and explicit inference pseudocode improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the reduced disclosure of known failure conditions and erroneous spectrogram axes, although those issues weaken the revision's presentation and qualification of its findings.
